traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT are implemented and verified by tests.
1) Core Functionality – @supports format - The `valid-annotation-format` rule, together with `valid-implements-utils`, fully supports the `@supports story-path REQ-ID1 REQ-ID2 ...` format. - Parsing is centralized in `validateImplementsAnnotationHelper` (via `parseImplementsTokens`), which splits the @supports value into a storyPath plus one-or-more requirement IDs. - Tests explicitly cover valid single and multi-line @supports usages, and invalid cases for missing values or missing requirement IDs.
2) Validation – requirements exist in specified story files - The `valid-req-reference` rule extends deep validation to @supports: - `parseImplementsLine` extracts storyPath and reqIds from @supports lines. - `validateImplementsLine` uses existing deep-validation infrastructure to resolve the story file, load its requirements, and assert that each reqId exists. - Jest tests confirm correct behavior for: - Valid @supports lines pointing to multi-story fixtures. - Missing requirements (reporting `reqMissing` with the appropriate storyPath). - Invalid @supports story paths (path traversal) for this mode.
3) Backward Compatibility – @story + @req unchanged - Story and requirement format validation logic for `@story` and `@req` remains in place and unmodified in spirit; @supports is added alongside, not replacing. - `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` tests confirm: - Functions without any traceability annotations are still reported as missing. - Functions with only legacy annotations behave as before. - The introduction of @supports is additive and does not change expectations for existing annotations, satisfying REQ-BACKWARD-COMP.
4) Mixed Usage – both styles, same codebase/file - `valid-annotation-format` explicitly supports mixed comments: its tests include a single block comment containing @story, @req, and @supports together and mark this as valid. - `valid-req-reference`’s `handleAnnotationLine` function processes @story, @req, and @supports lines in the same comment without conflict, sharing the same requirement cache. - Function-level rules (`require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`) accept either style, as demonstrated by tests where some functions use @story/@req and others only @supports in the same suite, with the correct results in each case.
5) Error Messages – story context included - For deep validation, the `reqMissing` message is `"Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'"`, and for each @supports line the correct storyPath from that line is passed through. Tests assert this data, which satisfies the requirement that error messages indicate which story was checked. - For format validation, `invalidImplementsFormat` messages use detailed `details` strings mentioning the problematic story path or the missing content, plus an example, as required by the story’s error-message examples.
6) Requirement Scoping – IDs unique only within story - Requirements are loaded and cached per *story file path* (`loadAndCacheRequirements` maps each resolved path to its own Set of REQ IDs), so the same REQ ID may exist in multiple story files without conflict. - Tests explicitly validate multi-story supports usage where `REQ-SHARED-ID` exists in two different story files and is accepted, proving IDs are scoped to their story file.
7) Quality Standards – ESLint rule best practices - All relevant rules (`valid-annotation-format`, `valid-req-reference`, `require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`) define proper `meta`, messages, and schemas. - Implementation is modularized into helpers (`valid-implements-utils`, `valid-annotation-format-*` helpers) and is extensively unit tested via Jest with clear requirement IDs and story references, matching ESLint rule development best practices.
8) Documentation – examples and migration guidance - The story file itself (docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md) includes: - Concrete examples of @supports usage for single and multiple stories. - Examples of the legacy @story + @req style. - Examples of mixed usage within a single function. - A migration strategy outlining how teams can progressively adopt @supports alongside existing annotations. This fulfills the documentation acceptance criterion for developers.
Given the existing implementation, targeted helper modules, and passing tests that directly reference and validate the behavior described in this story, the story 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT is fully implemented and verified in this codebase.
